m8-t1.question: What does a marketing portfolio have to prove that a résumé's skill list cannot?
options: That you know the terminology
Proof of work — decisions made and results achieved, with evidence
That you own a laptop
How many courses you have enrolled in
m8-t1.explanation: Marketing is a proof-of-work profession: case studies with problem, action, result and evidence — not claims.

m8-t1.question: What are the four PARE moves of a portfolio case study?
options: Product, price, place, promotion
Plan, act, report, evaluate
Problem, action, result, evidence
Preparation, audience, reach, engagement
m8-t1.explanation: PARE: honest problem paragraph, action as decisions, results with baselines, and screenshots/tables as evidence.

m8-t1.question: For an SEO Executive application, which exhibit should lead the portfolio?
options: The most visually attractive reel you made
The PB1 SEO audit with the crawl table and a before/after ranking screenshot
Your résumé's skill list
The certificate alone
m8-t1.explanation: Lead with the exhibit matching the role's #1 requirement — reorder the portfolio per application.

m8-t1.question: How do you handle the 'no experience' objection with course projects?
options: Describe them as agency internships
Inflate the budget numbers so they look professional
Reframe honestly: real local business, real constraints, documented results — plus one live client however small
Wait until you have a job to build a portfolio
m8-t1.explanation: Self-generated client work with real constraints and honest numbers IS experience — and one small live stakeholder upgrades every case study.

m8-t1.question: What does the ninety-second scan test check?
options: Whether the page loads fast
Whether a stranger can tell your target role in 10s, see a number-led result in 30s, and meet evidence twice in 90s
Whether you used a premium template
How many projects you have listed
m8-t1.explanation: Recruiters spend 60–120 seconds; the scroll order IS the pitch order — fix layout before content.

m8-t2.question: What is the résumé bullet pattern this lesson teaches?
options: Adjective + role + years of experience
Action verb + specific mechanism + result with number and baseline
Tool list + percentage growth
Company name + responsibilities
m8-t2.explanation: 'Audited a 40-page café site; fixed 23 crawl issues; organic clicks +34%' — verbs, mechanisms, measurable results.

m8-t2.question: Why must résumé keywords mirror the job description's exact terms?
options: To flatter the recruiter's vocabulary
Because applicant-tracking systems match literally — a beautiful PDF that never matches a keyword never meets a human
Because hiring managers skim only the first line
It doesn't matter; portfolios are all that count
m8-t2.explanation: ATS keyword matching is the first gate; mirror the posting's terms within honesty.

m8-t2.question: What makes a LinkedIn headline work for recruiter search?
options: Just your job title and company
An inspirational quote
Role keywords + proof + portfolio link — 'Digital Marketing Trainee | SEO audits, Meta Ads, GA4 dashboards | Portfolio: [link]'
Listing every tool you have ever opened
m8-t2.explanation: Recruiters search LinkedIn like a search engine; the headline is your title tag — keywords plus a click-through reason.

m8-t2.question: What is the honest way to present course-project numbers on a résumé?
options: Omit them; numbers invite questions
Present simulated results as real client work
Label them as course campaign (practice client) — honest labelling protects you when every bullet gets probed
Round them up to look stronger
m8-t2.explanation: Interviews probe every number; honest labels plus a strong story beat inflated claims that collapse under one question.

m8-t2.question: According to the lesson, what is the correct relationship between certifications and portfolio?
options: Certifications replace the need for a portfolio
Collect as many badges as possible; quantity signals dedication
Certifications are the garnish, not the meal — 'I have the cert, and here's the dashboard I built with it' is the whole game
Only paid certifications count
m8-t2.explanation: Skillshop, Blueprint, GA4 certs are worth having — but one cert plus one demo beats a wall of badges.

m8-t3.question: What does the marketing-adapted STAR-R add to the classic STAR pattern?
options: Rank — ordering your achievements
Reflection — what you'd do differently, after the Result
References — contacts who can vouch for you
Research — data about the company
m8-t3.explanation: Result with baselines, then the reflection beat — maturity interviewers read as judgment.

m8-t3.question: In the GSMAP case framework, what does the first move establish?
options: The channel plan
The budget split
The goal, KPIs and the guardrail (e.g., cost-per-order ceiling)
The creative concept
m8-t3.explanation: Goal & metrics first — then Situation & audience, Strategy & channel mix (70/20/10), Actions & timeline, Prediction & measurement.

m8-t3.question: What is the strongest trust signal available to a junior marketer in an interview?
options: Claiming every campaign succeeded
Confident body language
Honest failure analysis — miss, diagnosis, change, transfer
Knowing every tool's name
m8-t3.explanation: 'Everything worked' reads as 'never ran anything' — dissection of a real miss cannot be faked by someone who has never run anything.

m8-t3.question: The panel asks: 'A campaign's CPA doubled overnight. What do you do?' What is the correct first step?
options: Immediately cut the budget in half
Restart the campaign from scratch
Check tracking first, then bids/budget changes, then creative fatigue, then audience shifts, then the landing page
Blame the platform's algorithm
m8-t3.explanation: The diagnostic ladder from Lessons 4.4/6.4: rule out measurement before acting on the numbers.

m8-t3.question: Why should you end a case answer with 'happy to go deeper anywhere'?
options: To fill silence
To hide that you ran out of material
It invites the panel into your structure — a strength signal, where monologue is not
It is a traditional Indian interview custom
m8-t3.explanation: Cases grade structured thinking; the invitation shows confidence with the frame and collaboration over monologue.

questions.question: A recruiter gives your portfolio 90 seconds. Which page arrangement survives the scan?
options: Ten project thumbnails in a grid, click to explore
Identity block with target role, a lead case study with a number-led result line, evidence screenshots within two scrolls, contact and résumé link
A long 'about my journey' essay first, projects below
A skills cloud with animated percentages
questions.explanation: The ninety-second test: role clarity in 10s, a number-led result in 30s, evidence twice in 90s — scroll order IS pitch order.

questions.question: Two candidates, same skills listed. What makes one résumé get shortlisted from 340 applications?
options: A longer skills list
Specific verbs, mechanisms and numbers near the top — plus a portfolio link in the header
A colourful template
Mentioning passion for marketing twice
questions.explanation: The 6-second scan plus ATS keyword matching both reward specificity; the portfolio link is the differentiator.

questions.question: Case question: 'A Mangaluru dental clinic wants 30 enquiries/month on ₹15,000.' Which answer opens correctly?
options: I'd start with Instagram reels — dental content does well
First, the goal and guardrail: 30 enquiries means CPA ≤ ₹500; leading indicators are map actions, calls and form fills — then I'd audit their listing and review presence before spending
I'd split the budget equally across five channels for safety
I'd ask for a bigger budget first
questions.explanation: GSMAP: establish metrics and the guardrail, diagnose the situation, THEN choose channels — structure before tactics.

questions.question: An interviewer asks 'Tell me about a campaign that didn't work.' Which answer helps you most?
options: Honestly, all my campaigns achieved their goals

My display-ad test spent ₹1,800 for 3 enquiries — my worst CPA; diagnosis: audience too broad, I ignored intent evidence; I killed it in week 2 and wrote a rule in the log; now I demand intent proof before any spend
The platform's algorithm changed, so it wasn't my fault
I prefer to focus on my successes
questions.explanation: Miss, diagnosis, change, transfer — the four-name pattern is the trust signal that cannot be faked.

questions.question: Your LinkedIn has 12 skills but the profile shows no Featured items and no posts. What does this signal to a recruiter?
options: Humility — letting the work speak
A contradiction: 'active practitioner' claims with a spectator's profile — pin three case studies and post weekly results
Nothing; LinkedIn profiles are rarely checked
That you are focused on your current job
questions.explanation: LinkedIn is SEO on yourself: keyword headline, proof-first About, Featured exhibits, and consistency that signals a practitioner.

questions.question: Which set of five STAR-R stories covers 90% of behavioural marketing questions?
options: Five stories about teamwork from college fests
One SEO audit, one content engine, one paid campaign, one analytics decision, one community/crisis handling — all from real project work
Five different tool tutorials you completed
One story told five different ways
questions.explanation: Map the stories to the craft's pillars — interviewers ask differently; you answer from the same shelf.

questions.question: In a case answer, where does the 70/20/10 budget logic belong?
options: Before establishing the goal — it is the universal rule
In the Strategy & channel mix step: core channel for the bulk, proven secondary, and one experiment — justified by the audience evidence gathered in the previous step
In the final prediction, as a hedge
Nowhere; 70/20/10 is only for existing accounts
questions.explanation: GSMAP's third move: the mix follows goal and situation — never precedes them.

questions.question: 'How do you measure content that doesn't convert directly?' Which answer shows Module 6 mastery?
options: You can't; content is a branding exercise
Count likes and impressions as proxies
Assisted conversions, brand-search volume, saves and shares as leading indicators — and the how-did-you-hear log as the model-free truth-teller, with a pause test if the budget is significant
Only measure direct sales from UTM links
questions.explanation: Attribution honesty plus incrementality checks — the full 6.4 toolkit applied to content's indirect role.

questions.question: When the interviewer asks 'Do you have questions for us?', what does the lesson recommend?
options: Say 'no, you covered everything' to signal satisfaction
Ask about salary immediately as the first question
Two operator questions: what the first 90 days look like, and how the team decides where budget goes / the review rhythm
Ask a trivia question about the company's founding year
questions.explanation: Both questions prove you think like an operator — onboarding and measurement rhythm, the two things a marketer manages.

questions.question: What turns interview readiness from talent into skill, per the lesson?
options: Natural confidence and extroversion
The rehearsal protocol: answers practised aloud, timed case questions recorded and reviewed, mock loops with partners, and a scorecard tracked like the weekly ritual
Memorising answers word for word
Watching interview videos the night before
questions.explanation: The mouth needs practice the brain cannot substitute — aloud, timed, recorded, scored, and improved one fix at a time.
